questions.q: A sample of $4 . 5mg$ of an unknown monohydric alcohol, $R - OH$ was added to methylmagnesium iodide. A gas is evolved and is collected and its volume measured to be $3 . 1mL$. The molecular weight of the unknown alcohol is $g / mol$.
questions.solution:
Alcohols on reaction with Grignard reagent forms hydrocarbons.This is due to the presence of active hydrogen in alcohols and here grignard reagent acts as a base.

When any alcohol is treated with methyl magnemsium iodide the hydrocarbon formed should be methane gas.

$ROH + {CH}_{3}MgI \to ROMgI + {CH}_{4}\left(g\right)$

Number of moles of ${CH}_{4} =$ Number of moles of $ROH$

$⇒ \dfrac{Volume ( Litres ) ofthegas}{22400} = \dfrac{massofthegas}{Molecularmassofthegas}$ (Assuming $NTP$ Condition)

$⇒ \dfrac{3 . 1}{22400} = \dfrac{4 . 5 \times {10}^{- 3}}{Molecularmassofthegas}$

$⇒ MM = 32 . 51$

$= 33$$g / mol$

questions.q:
$0 . 25g$ of an organic compound containing chlorine gave $0 . 40g$ of silver chloride in Carius estimation. The percentage of chlorine present in the compound is [in nearest integer]
(Given: Molar mass of $Ag$ is $108g{mol}^{- 1}$ and that of $Cl$ is $35 . 5g{mol}^{- 1}$)
questions.solution:
Percentage of chlorine in the organic compound=$\dfrac{atomicmassofchlorineXmassofAgClformedX100}{molecularmassofAgClXweightoforganiccompound}$

Mass of organic compound $= 0 . 25g$

Mass of $AgCl$ formed $= 0 . 40g$

Mass of $Cl$ in organic compound $= \dfrac{0 . 40 \times 35 . 5}{143 . 5 \times 0 . 25}$

Percentage of $Cl$ in the compound $= \dfrac{0 . 40 \times 35 . 5}{143 . 5 \times 0 . 25} \times 100$

$= 39 . 58 %$

Nearest integer=40.

questions.q: $0 . 2g$ of an organic compound was subjected to estimation of nitrogen by Dumas method in which volume of ${N}_{2}$ evolved (at STP) was found to be $22 . 400mL$. The percentage of nitrogen in the compound is - [nearest integer] (Given: Molar mass of ${N}_{2}$ is $28g{mol}^{- 1}$, Molar volume of ${N}_{2}$ at $STP: 22 . 4L$)
questions.solution:
Volume of N2 gas is equal to 22.4 ml at STP
Mole of N2 gas = $\dfrac{22 . 4}{22400} = \dfrac{1}{1000}$
Weight of N2 gas =$\dfrac{1}{1000}X28$

% of N in organic compound $=$$\dfrac{28}{1000}X\dfrac{100}{0 . 2} = 14 %$

Hence, The percentage of nitrogen in the compound is 14%

questions.q: In bromination of Propyne, with Bromine $1, 1, 2, 2$-tetrabromopropane is obtained in $27 %$ yield. The amount of $1, 1, 2, 2$ tetrabromopropane obtained from $1g$ of Bromine in this reaction is_____$\times {10}^{- 1}g$ . (Molar Mass : Bromine $= 80g / mol$)
questions.solution:
According to the above chemical reaction, 2 moles of bromine will give one mole of the product.

2 moles of ${Br}_{2} = 2 \times 160gof{Br}_{2}givesonemoleofproduct = 360gofproduct$

So, mass of product formed from $1gmof{Br}_{2}willbe = \dfrac{360}{2 \times 160} \times 1g = \dfrac{9}{8}gofproduct$

But given that % yield = 27%.

So actual amount of product $= \dfrac{9}{8} \times \dfrac{27}{100} = 0 . 30gram$

$= 3 . 0 \times {10}^{- 1}g$
